fixture.seed: Not encoded in this immutable captured public snapshot; no simulation is run.

workload.method: Fixed public snapshot and pinned presentation code. Serial gl.finish() was attempted as a completion boundary but returned near-zero despite long callback intervals; it did not establish GPU or display completion. Measured values are callback intervals, JavaScript update/submission durations and gl.finish call duration. Warmup rows and long intervals are retained; screenshots establish final captured pixels only.

measurementInterpretation.valid: interval is the wall-clock gap between starts of measured render callbacks. updateMs and submissionMs are JavaScript-side timings. Screenshots prove that the final captured scene produced real pixels.
measurementInterpretation.completionNotEstablished: gl.finish returned in 0.0–0.3 ms despite 400–1600 ms callback gaps. This probe did not validate GPU execution or compositor completion per sample. completedWorkMs is a historical field name for update + render submission + gl.finish call duration, NOT GPU-completed frame duration. rawFrames, warmupCompletedFrames and measuredCompletedFrames likewise count callbacks, not proven displayed frames.
measurementInterpretation.limits: 20 samples per case, one serial ordering, one fixed snapshot, shared CPU host; p99 equals worst by nearest-rank. No sustained-frame-rate or hardware-GPU claim. Warmup waits for texture/environment readiness and five callbacks, not validated shader completion.

measurementCorrection: Historical field names completedWorkMs, completed frames and measuredCompletedFrames refer to JavaScript durations and callback counts. They must not be interpreted as GPU-completed or displayed-frame timing.
